title: GH-600 practice bank · set 4 (all question formats)
author: Claude, checked against GitHub Docs (November 2026). Covers every question format the simulator supports.

questions.stem:
Contoso enables GitHub Copilot cloud agent on `contoso/orders-api`. The default branch is protected by a ruleset that requires one approving review.

For each of the following statements, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.

items.statement: The cloud agent can push commits directly to the default branch.
items.explanation: The agent can only push to branches it creates (`copilot/…`) and works through pull requests.

items.statement: Workflows on a pull request opened by the cloud agent wait for a user with write access to approve them before they run.
items.explanation: By default, GitHub Actions workflows don't run automatically on the agent's pull requests; someone with write access approves them.

items.statement: The developer who asked Copilot to create the pull request can approve it to satisfy the required review.
items.explanation: The person who asked Copilot to create a pull request can't approve it, which keeps the required-approvals control independent.

questions.takeaway: Agent: own branch only, its CI runs need approval, and the requester can't be the approver.

questions.scenario:
This question is part of a series of questions that present the same scenario. Each question in the series contains a unique solution that might meet the stated goals.

CODEOWNERS in `contoso/orders-api` contains a single line: `* @contoso/developers`. The ruleset on `main` requires one approving review. Agents open pull requests that sometimes change files under `.github/workflows/`.

**Goal:** a change under `.github/workflows/` must not be merged without approval from `@contoso/platform`.

items.solution: Add `/.github/workflows/ @contoso/platform` on a new line **after** the existing line, and turn on "Require review from Code Owners" in the ruleset.
items.explanation: The last matching pattern wins, so the new line owns workflow files, and the code owner review rule makes that approval mandatory.
Instructions are guidance; nothing blocks the merge if the agent edits a workflow anyway.

items.solution: Add `/.github/workflows/ @contoso/platform` as the **first** line of CODEOWNERS, and turn on "Require review from Code Owners" in the ruleset.
items.explanation: The `*` line comes later and matches everything, so it overrides the workflow line; developers remain the owners.

questions.takeaway: Problem-solution sets: judge each solution on its own. CODEOWNERS needs the right order and the code owner review rule.

questions.stem:
You need to add a GitHub Agentic Workflow that produces a weekly repository report. The repository doesn't use Agentic Workflows yet.

Which five actions should you perform in sequence?

items.text: Install the `gh aw` extension for the GitHub CLI.
Write the workflow as a Markdown file in `.github/workflows/`, with triggers, permissions and safe outputs in the frontmatter.
Run `gh aw compile` to generate the `.lock.yml` workflow.
Commit both the `.md` file and the generated `.lock.yml` file.
Trigger the workflow and review the issue it creates.
Edit the `.lock.yml` file by hand to add the steps the agent needs.
Add the agent to the ruleset bypass list so its outputs aren't blocked.

questions.explanation: The Markdown file is the source and the compiler generates the lock file that GitHub Actions runs, so both are committed together. Hand-editing the lock file is overwritten by the next compile, and the bypass list is never the answer for agents.
questions.takeaway: Agentic Workflows: author Markdown → compile → commit .md and .lock.yml → run.

questions.stem:
You are designing guardrails for agents in `contoso/orders-api`.

Which control should you use for each requirement? To answer, select the appropriate control for each requirement.

targets.text: Block merging until the `build` and `test` jobs succeed.
targets.rationale: Required status checks gate the merge on CI results.

targets.text: Define who must review changes to files under `infra/`.
targets.rationale: CODEOWNERS maps paths to owners; the ruleset's code owner review rule makes their approval mandatory.

targets.text: Pause a production deployment until the operations team approves it.
targets.rationale: Environment required reviewers hold the deploy job before it runs.

targets.text: Deny the shell command `az group delete` before the agent runs it.
targets.rationale: A `preToolUse` hook inspects each tool call and can deny it with a reason.

targets.text: Limit which external hosts the cloud agent can reach during its session.
targets.rationale: The firewall restricts the agent's outbound network access to an allowlist.

questions.explanation: Each control acts at a different point: merge (rulesets, CODEOWNERS), deployment (environments), tool execution (hooks) and network (firewall). Safe outputs aren't used here; they constrain what an Agentic Workflow may write.
questions.takeaway: Match the control to the moment it acts: merge, deploy, tool call or network.

questions.title: Case study: Northwind Traders
questions.scenario:
### Overview
Northwind Traders builds its ordering platform in .NET and hosts it on Azure. The code is in the GitHub organisation `northwind`, mainly in the repository `northwind/platform`.

### Existing environment
- Deployments run from `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` and authenticate to Azure with a client secret stored as the Actions repository secret `AZURE_CREDENTIALS`.
- Developers have the Write role on `northwind/platform`.
- GitHub Copilot cloud agent is enabled for the organisation.

### Requirements
- Developers will assign issues to the cloud agent.
- Deployments must stop using stored long-lived Azure credentials.
- A weekly dependency report must be created as an issue by an AI agent, without giving the agent write access to the repository.

questions.stem: For each of the following statements, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.

items.statement: Developers with the Write role can assign issues in `northwind/platform` to the cloud agent.
items.explanation: Users with write access to the repository can assign work to Copilot cloud agent, provided it's enabled for them.

items.statement: The cloud agent can read `AZURE_CREDENTIALS` during its session.
items.explanation: The cloud agent doesn't have access to Actions secrets; only secrets configured under Agents.

items.statement: To authenticate to Azure with OpenID Connect, the deploy job needs the `id-token: write` permission.
items.explanation: The job must be allowed to request an OIDC token from GitHub.

questions.takeaway: Write access assigns work; Agents secrets only; OIDC needs id-token: write.

questions.stem: Which approach meets the requirement for the weekly dependency report?

options.text: A scheduled workflow that runs Copilot CLI with `issues: write` and `contents: write`.
options.rationale: Incorrect. The agent itself would hold write access, which the requirement forbids.

options.text: Assign a recurring issue to the cloud agent every Monday.
options.rationale: Incorrect. The cloud agent writes to the repository through branches and pull requests, and nothing here schedules it.

options.text: A GitHub Agentic Workflow on a weekly schedule with read-only permissions and a `create-issue` safe output.
options.rationale: Correct. The agent only proposes the issue; a separate safe-output job validates and creates it, so the agent never has write access.

options.text: A Dependabot configuration with weekly version updates.
options.rationale: Incorrect. Dependabot opens update pull requests; it isn't an AI-written report issue.

questions.explanation: Safe outputs separate the agent's proposal from the write action, which a deterministic job performs with only the permission it needs.
questions.takeaway: AI that must create things without write access → Agentic Workflow + safe outputs.
